doc.title: Bernie Kirsh interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 27, 2022

chapter: Music beginnings and entering the studio
title: Growing up in Philadelphia playing brass
summary: Midway through college in 1966, Kirsh recalls playing trombone and baritone horn and the strong Philadelphia school music program. A short aside about computer fan hiss follows.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Yeah. You just do them. And I’m going to ask you a little bit about that but I wanted to start with a little scenario. You and I are fairly close together in age and I was looking at the top songs of 1966 and I was thinking of you, if my stats are correct you were mid- way through college around then?
Yeah, ’66 I was, yeah, that’s right. Mid-way through college. Yeah.

Yeah. And the playlist top songs of that year included everyone from the Mamas and the Papas, The Beatles, Ray Conniff, The Monkees, and Frank Sinatra. So were you a person who listened to music by this point, noticing things that the average listener did not?

I don’t know. I don’t know what the average listener is listening to, but I mean my interest was not listening for anything in particular, it was just enjoying the music. I started out as a musician playing, you know, through I guess grade school, junior high school, started playing brass instruments, trombone, baritone horn, that sort of thing. Always had an interest in my life that I never really fulfilled totally to my liking of keyboard/piano playing. But the brass instruments, and the trombone in particular, were © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-

my way into a musical life and that consisted of all of the things you do in school, in high school, and around them. I grew up in Philadelphia, which had a great music program by the way. There were some wonderful people there and a great curriculum. And in high school you get theory of harmony, counterpoint, composition — in high school. And they had the All-City programs. So my interest was in playing music. I enjoyed it.
I’m going to pause for a second. I’m not pausing, but I’m getting a sort of a hiss every time you speak. Do you know what that might be?
You know what? I think it’s the fan in this. I don’t know.
Yeah ‘cause I can hear the fan going. I’m not sure.
Oh it’s the fan in the computer?
In the computer. It’s a laptop. Yeah.
Okay. It’s not bad. I have a guy who can maybe do some tweaking.
